The related work has been conducted by many researchers, for instance, Zhai and Sun [1,2] conducted pioneering work on parameters optimization to improve the wheel/rail dynamic interactions based on a vertical vehicle–track interaction model; Kaewunruen and Remennikov [3] presented an SA to analyze the free vibrations of an in situ concrete sleeper, in which the influence of variation of rail-pad parameters on the behavior of sleepers is identified, and similar works are presented in Refs. [4] and [5]; for assessing the effects of the inertial properties of railway vehicles on their dynamic responses, Suarez et al. [6] performed dynamic simulations accounting for the masses, moments of inertia, and heights of the center of gravity of the car body, bogie, and wheelset one at a time; Zakeri et al. [7] considered the coupled vertical and roll vibrations of a horizontally curved bridge to analyze the SA of the variables, e.g., cant, train speed, track quality, radius of curvature, etc.

However, one should realize a fact that though one or several track irregularity types form the most sensitive group to the dynamic responses of system components, the FOSI or the total sensitive index is varied against time, as shown in Figs. 5(a) and 6(a), due to the intrinsically time-varying amplitude–frequency characteristics of track irregularities.
